Evidence: Local tier reads/writes registry record.mountPath (service:167, 303-312) while the PG tier reads/writes workspaces.metadata.customMountPath (service:194, 323-336). Nothing copies between the two; the registry path is only used on a PG connection error (service:216-219).
Reproduction: Attach a workspace mount with no DATABASE_URL (local tier), then set DATABASE_URL and resolve the same workspace: mountedPath is null although the mount was configured; and vice versa.
Root cause: Two storage tiers for the same logical field with no sync, no migration, and no conflict rule; tier choice is an env-time branch, not a per-record state.
Impact: A configured mount silently disappears (or reappears) when the deployment tier changes; panel and agents agree with each other but the user's mount is gone.
Proposed fix: Pick one truth (proposal: registry record.mountPath is local truth; PG metadata.customMountPath is a mirror) and add read-time backfill plus a one-shot migration; document in Domain Spec Owns/Ports.
Required tests: PG-gated attach/resolve round-trip in both tiers; tier-flip characterization test (T1, T2).
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-cm-micro-001-002): service read-time backfill both ways + write-through attach/clear; tests channel-mount-tier-flip.test.ts (T1/T2)

Evidence: getAllowedRoots catches getWorkspaceRecord failure (.catch(() => null), service:57) and falls through to defaultRoots() = [sandbox, os.homedir()] (service:48-54). readAllRaw swallows ALL read/parse errors to [] (registry:245-248), so a corrupt registry looks like no-record.
Reproduction: Write a workspace record with allowedMountRoots: [narrow], corrupt workspaces.json (invalid JSON or unreadable), call allowedRoots(wsId) or validate(path, wsId): the jail widens to sandbox+home instead of failing closed.
Root cause: Read-error and no-record are conflated; the policy default is the WIDE jail, so an unreadable registry silently widens every workspace's mount scope.
Impact: A registry read failure (corruption, permissions, partial write) lets mounts outside the intended per-workspace jail validate and attach.
Proposed fix: Distinguish no-record (default policy) from unreadable (fail closed: [sandboxBase] or explicit error); have readAllRaw surface a typed error instead of [] for parse failures.
Required tests: Corrupt-registry test asserting the jail does NOT widen (T3).
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07 (fix-cm-micro-001-002): service:57 fail-closed + workspace-registry.ts:247 throw; test channel-mount-tier-flip.test.ts (T3)

Evidence: Routes take :id from the URL and call the gate with no comparison against request.workspaceId / x-workspace-id; the only gates are global (pinGate, authGate loopback-trust, tenant DB hook). GET/PUT mount, browse and allowed-roots all accept any id.
Reproduction: Send PUT /api/workspaces/<other-ws>/mount (or channel/category id of another workspace) with a valid x-workspace-id header for a different workspace: the write succeeds; GET returns the other workspace's mount path and jail roots.
Root cause: Domain trusts the id in the path; ownership is never resolved or checked, and loopback callers are keyless by design.
Impact: In a multi-tenant install any reachable client can read and rewrite other workspaces' mount columns (and see their host paths), by id.
Proposed fix: Resolve the target's owning workspace (channelGate.get / getCategory / workspace record) and require it to match request.workspaceId; 403 otherwise. Confirm intended single-user blast radius first (User Decision).
Required tests: Cross-workspace PUT/GET test expecting 403 after fix (T5).
Status: Fixed-verified 2026-10-07: gate port channelMountGate.owns (channel-mount-service.ts:109; gate:58) + route guards GET/PUT channels/categories/workspaces (routes/channel-mounts.ts:72,81,97,106,134,143) and browse/allowed-roots (routes:40,57); regression src/channel-mounts/channel-mount-gate.test.ts:731-796 (T5); npx vitest run src/channel-mounts 59/59 + tsc clean

Evidence: refuseWorkspaceVfs walks up at most 4 levels (for depth < 4) looking for a basename === 'vfs' with markers (.crowdos dir or sibling workspace.json).
Reproduction: Fixture <sandbox>/<ws>/vfs/a/b/c/d/e; validate(<sandbox>/<ws>/vfs/a/b/c/d/e, wsId) with a jail containing the sandbox: valid=true, so a mount can point inside the workspace config sandbox.
Root cause: Depth-limited upward walk: targets more than 4 segments below vfs/ never reach the checked ancestor.
Impact: The vfs/ refusal (canon: workspace runtime state is never a mount target) is bypassable at depth; a mount there lets a repo and workspace config overlap.
Proposed fix: Walk to the filesystem root (or to the nearest allowed root) instead of a fixed depth; keep the marker check.

Evidence: catPromise/wsPromise are started eagerly; when the channel-level path validates, resolveChannelMount returns without awaiting them (service:361-366). resolveWorkspaceMount rethrows non-connection errors (service:217), so the floating wsPromise can reject with no handler.
Reproduction: Make resolveWorkspaceMount throw a non-connection error (e.g. a drizzle logic error) for a channel with a valid folderPath: the request succeeds but the abandoned promise rejects; process guards log an unhandledRejection and a DB query is wasted.
Root cause: Eager prefetch combined with early return; no .catch attached to the abandoned promises.
Impact: Noise/leak under DB logic errors; extra DB work per resolved channel request.
Proposed fix: Attach .catch(() => null) to prefetch promises, or defer prefetch until needed.
Required tests: Fault-injection test (mock resolveWorkspaceMount rejection) asserting no unhandled rejection (part of T1 harness).

Evidence: Local: getWorkspaceRecord is served from a 60s recordCache (registry:268-272) and saveWorkspaceRecord rewrites the WHOLE record from that snapshot (registry:301-315). PG: metadata is read into currentMeta then written back wholesale (service:319-336).
Reproduction: Two concurrent writers to the same workspace record (e.g. attachWorkspace + workspace rename/rename allowedMountRoots, or two metadata writers): the second save reverts the first's field; for PG, concurrent metadata writers lose one side.
Root cause: Read-modify-write outside a compare-and-swap; the registry lock serializes writes but not the read-modify-write window, and the record cache serves stale snapshots.
Impact: Lost updates on workspace records/metadata when mount writes race other writers (single-user: rare; automation/worker: possible).
Proposed fix: Re-read inside the registry lock (no cache) for mount writes, or add a targeted patch API (set mountPath only) instead of whole-record save; PG: jsonb_set-style single-key update or a transaction.
Required tests: Concurrent-attach test asserting no field reversion (T6).

Evidence: attachChannel/attachCategory wrap gate calls in .catch(() => null) and map everything to generic 'Failed to set/clear ...' (service:444, 450, 459, 465); updateCategory returns null for BOTH not-found and local write miss (channel-local-store.ts:210).
Reproduction: Inject a store write failure during attachCategory: the user sees 'Failed to clear the category mount' with no cause; a missing row and a broken store are indistinguishable.
Root cause: Broad catch + generic message discards the underlying error; null return conflates two outcomes.
Impact: Diagnosis time; UI cannot tell 'gone' from 'broken' (the 2026-09-23 fix only stopped false success).
Proposed fix: Preserve the cause (message/code) in the error string or return a typed failure; distinguish not-found from store-failure.
Required tests: Store-failure injection test asserting distinct messages (T13).

Evidence: setEffectiveMounts resolves channel -> category -> workspace; an unknown channelId with a valid workspaceId silently falls through to the workspace branch and writes the workspace set (service:634-662). Test only covers missing channelId with NO workspaceId (channel-mount-chain.test.ts:224-227).
Reproduction: Call setEffectiveMounts({ workspaceId: 'ws-1', channelId: 'ch-missing', mounts }) -> { ok: true } and the workspace runtime object is overwritten.
Root cause: Missing ids are treated as 'level not present' instead of 'caller named a level that does not exist'.
Impact: A typo'd channel id overwrites the workspace-wide default mounts - the highest-blast-radius level.
Proposed fix: When an id is provided but the row is missing, return { ok: false, error } instead of falling through.

Evidence: resolveMountScope computes workspaceRoot = resolveWorkspaceLocalRoot(input.workspaceId) (service:285), ignoring the effectiveWorkspaceId the resolver derived from the channel (service:248).
Reproduction: Call scope({ channelId: 'ch-of-ws-X' }) with no workspaceId: path/zone/source describe ws-X's mount, but workspaceRoot is the sandbox base (resolveWorkspaceLocalRoot(null), registry:163).
Root cause: Two different workspace derivations in one method: effectiveRoot derives the workspace from the channel; workspaceRoot uses only the raw input.
Impact: The Repo panel's 'Zone A sibling' link can point at the sandbox base instead of the workspace's own directory when only channelId is supplied.
Proposed fix: Resolve effectiveWorkspaceId once (channel's workspace when input omitted) and use it for both.

Evidence: Local tier persists v.resolved with backslashes replaced by '/' (service:311); PG tier persists v.resolved native (service:334). resolveMountScope/displayName and panel headers read the stored string.
Reproduction: On win32: attach via local tier (C:/Users/...), then switch to PG tier and attach again (C:\\Users\\...); stored forms differ, and any exact-string consumer sees two different paths.
Root cause: Normalization applied on one tier only; no canonical form at the contract boundary.
Impact: Mixed-separator ambiguity on win32 across tiers; tests only assert the local slash form.
Proposed fix: Normalize once in the gate/service (forward slashes) for both tiers, or store canonical and convert at the edges; add a win32 round-trip test.

Evidence: readdir(realDir, { withFileTypes: true }) materializes every entry, then filter/map/sort run over all of them, and only afterwards filtered.slice(0, 300).
Reproduction: Browse a directory with >100k entries: the route does full readdir + sort work before the 300 cap.
Root cause: Cap applied after materialization; no early termination possible with a global sort, but the uncapped work is the issue.
Impact: Latency/memory spike on pathological directories in the picker; no security impact.
Proposed fix: Keep the cap but bound work (e.g. readdir with limit where available, or document the cost); optionally stream/top-k.

Evidence: realpath results are cached 60s/200 keys; validate and browse trust the cached realpath for containment.
Reproduction: Retarget a symlink from inside the jail to outside it; within 60s validate(symlink) still reports valid against the old realpath.
Root cause: Positive-result cache with no invalidation hook on the filesystem.
Impact: Bounded TOCTOU-lite window (<=60s) where containment is evaluated on a stale realpath.
Proposed fix: Cache negative/positive with a shorter TTL for symlinks, or re-realpath when the candidate is a symlink; document the window.

Evidence: Read path: resolveWorkspaceMount catches connection errors and falls back to the registry record (service:216-219). Write path: attachWorkspaceMount PG branch calls db.update with no try/catch, so a connection error rejects (service:315-337).
Reproduction: Stop the DB (or use an unreachable DATABASE_URL), then PUT /api/workspaces/:id/mount: read works (registry fallback), attach returns an unhandled 500.
Root cause: Write path lacks the fallback the read path has; asymmetry between read and write tier policies.
Impact: Mount changes fail mid-outage even though reads keep serving - the user cannot re-point a mount while the DB is down.
Proposed fix: Mirror the read fallback: on connection error, write the registry record (and queue convergence) or return a typed degraded result.

Evidence: Workspace branch builds workspaceSet with mode 'default' unconditionally (service:664), even if input.mode was 'inherit' or 'override'; the return echoes the coerced set.
Reproduction: Call setEffectiveMounts({ workspaceId, mounts, mode: 'inherit' }) -> returns mode 'default'; caller cannot store an inherit at workspace level (probably intended) but is not told.
Root cause: Coercion without validation; 'inherit' at workspace level is meaningless but silently accepted.
Impact: API surprise; callers cannot distinguish accepted-with-coercion from honored input.
Proposed fix: Reject invalid workspace modes with { ok: false, error } (like the channel/category 'default' refusal) or document the coercion in the gate contract.

Evidence: effectiveMounts/setEffectiveMounts have no route, socket, or client caller (grep across packages: only tests). The docs list this as a known gap.
Reproduction: Search for channelMountGate.effectiveMounts outside tests: none; canon fsMounts resolve only from seeded data.
Root cause: Feature shipped at service+gate level without transport/UI.
Impact: Maintenance surface with no user; drift risk between canon mounts and host mounts.
Proposed fix: Decide: add transport + client (with contract tests) or remove the canon surface; either way update Domain Spec Gaps.

Evidence: pick-folder-win32.ps1 is referenced nowhere (route hard-410s, routes/channel-mounts.ts:36-38). ChannelMountRecord/CategoryMountRecord/FsBrowseEntry are exported but unused and not re-exported by the gate.
Reproduction: Grep for pick-folder-win32.ps1 / ChannelMountRecord: no production consumers.
Root cause: Assets left behind after the server picker was removed; record types predate the current shape.
Impact: Dead weight; docs must track unused exports (already listed as a gap).
Proposed fix: Delete the .ps1 and unused types, or wire them; keep the 410 route with a plain schema.

Evidence: Category attach emits category:mount-updated with payload { categoryId, ...info } and NO workspaceId and NO options channelId (routes:72). broker.onAny then has no channelId and no payloadWorkspaceId, so it takes the global branch: every workspace room (and, when origins include localhost/'*', a global io.emit) receives the event (register-socket-server.ts:447-459).
Reproduction: With two workspaces connected, attach a category mount in ws-A; sockets in ws-B receive category:mount-updated including the host path in the payload.
Root cause: The category route cannot derive workspaceId from the payload it builds; the fan-out treats 'no scope' as 'global'.
Impact: Cross-workspace leakage of mount metadata (absolute host paths) in multi-workspace installs.
Proposed fix: Include workspaceId (category's workspace) in the emit, and make the socket fan-out drop or scope unscoped mount events instead of broadcasting globally.

Location: re-docs/Backend Docs/Domain Spec/ChannelMounts.md:33-41; re-docs/Backend Docs/Feature and Flow Spec/Mount resolution flow.md:8-20
Evidence: Docs cite service line ranges that no longer match (e.g. getAllowedRoots 'channel-mount-service.ts:38-57' vs actual 47-66; 'channel-mount-service.ts:479' for allowedRoots vs actual 530; resolveEffectiveRoot '188-231' vs actual 233-276). AGENTS.md §6 requires docs sync in the same task as code changes.
Reproduction: Open the cited lines: they point at unrelated code or shifted ranges.
Root cause: Line-number citations were not refreshed after the last service edits.
Impact: Reviewers following docs land on wrong code; the 'code is truth' contract is weakened.
Proposed fix: Refresh citations (prefer symbol names + ranges) when the domain is next touched; keep the known-gaps list current.

Evidence: The category emit passes only { categoryId, ...info }; unlike the workspace emit (routes:90) it omits workspaceId, so even a fan-out fix at the socket layer cannot scope it from the payload.
Reproduction: Inspect the emitted payload for category:mount-updated: no workspaceId field; MountInfo.workspaceId exists but is nested and the socket layer reads only payload.workspaceId (register-socket-server.ts:416).
Root cause: Route builds the payload without the scope the socket layer needs.
Impact: Same leak as CM-017; also makes debugging scoping harder.
Proposed fix: Spread info and add workspaceId explicitly (info.workspaceId ?? resolved category workspace).

Evidence: wsPromise is only created when channel.workspaceId is set; when it is null the workspace level is never consulted, and the category's own workspace (cat.workspaceId) is not used to resolve a workspace mount either.
Reproduction: Channel with workspaceId null whose category has workspaceId set to a workspace that has a mountPath: resolve(channelId) returns none even though the category's workspace mount exists.
Root cause: The workspace fallback keys off channel.workspaceId only; the category is consulted for folderPath but not for its workspace.
Impact: A category-scoped workspace mount is invisible to channels with null workspaceId (legacy/unscoped rows).
Proposed fix: Fall back to cat.workspaceId for the workspace-mount lookup when channel.workspaceId is null.

Evidence: If realpath fails, validate falls back to real = resolved (unresolved path) and still runs containment on it; a symlinked component whose realpath errors (e.g. EACCES on an ancestor) is compared as-is.
Reproduction: Construct a path whose realpath throws but whose lexical form is inside the jail: validate may accept the lexical form while the real target differs.
Root cause: realpath failure is treated as 'use the raw path' instead of 'reject'.
Impact: Weaker symlink safety in an error path; low likelihood.
Proposed fix: Reject on realpath failure, or re-stat components; never containment-check an unresolved path.

Evidence: Clear-without-validate detach; pick-folder hard 410 (desktop owns the dialog); route emits wrapped in empty catch (best-effort notification, mount write is the commit point).
Reproduction: Review: detach on a missing/outside path succeeds by design; POST /api/fs/pick-folder always 410; a broker outage does not fail the attach.
Root cause: Deliberate product decisions documented in Domain Spec/Feature docs.
Impact: No defect; recorded so future audits do not 'fix' them by accident.
Proposed fix: Keep as-is; re-confirm only if multi-user requirements change.
